Go with my application and make the ------- 1. Navigation Hierarchy & Role Architecture
For ANM & CHO (Field Mobile App):

Page 1 (First Screen): Add Case — Opens immediately to the streamlined registration form.
Page 2: Dashboard — High-level field triage, urgent counts, and cluster status.
Page 3: Follow-ups — "Follow-up to be done" panel enabled whenever lists are assigned/inserted from Block/District for their jurisdiction.


For Block Nodal Authority (HRP Helpdesk Head) & also same for BHM :

Page 1 (First Screen): Dashboard — Centralized block-wide surveillance, three-track scheduling triangulation, and urgent queue.
Page 2: Follow-up to be done — Comprehensive All Persons Panel with shared status tracking across all referred HRP cases.
Page 3 (Last Screen): Add HRP Case — Facility/helpdesk intake form.
Page 4 (USING WHICH HE CAN ASSIGN OR CREATE THE ROLE LIKE HRP HELPDESK USING EMAIL AND PASSWORD ETC AND THEN ONLY THAT PERSON USING THAT CREDENTIALS CAN ACCESS THE THINGS )

2. ANM / CHO First Page: FIRST ONLY ADD BUTTON OVER THE WHOLE PAGE OTHER WISE SOME CRITICAL INSTRUCTION WHICH IS GOING TO COME AT THE BOTTOM - LIKE SYNC NOW , OR ONE HRP NEEDS FOLLOW UP URGENTLY LIKE THAT -- AFTER CLICKING ON THAT BIG ADD BUTTON - THEN Simplified 7-Field Intake Form
 Captured strictly with only the 7 requested fields:

Name: Mother's Full Name (with Aadhaar / MCP label guidance).
Mobile Number: Clean 10-digit number field with +91 country prefix.
Age: Completed years integer input.
Village (mapped to HWC): Dropdown mapped directly to the local Health & Wellness Sub-Center.
LMP (Last Menstrual Period): Date picker that automatically calculates and badges Estimated Date of Delivery (EDD) and gestational age.
Complication Dropdown: Exact specified options:
Anemia
PIH (Pregnancy-Induced Hypertension)
GDM (Gestational Diabetes Mellitus)
Short stature
Pre-LSCS
Multi gravida
Twins / Multiple Pregnancy
Teenage Pregnancy
Edema

Referring or Not?: Radio toggle between:
Yes - Refer to CHC/FRU (escalates to Block Nodal HRP Helpdesk network and also on BHM panel )
No - Routine Field Management (managed at village HSC cluster)
3. ANM & CHO "Follow-up to be done" Panel & Timelines
Screen: ANM / CHO 3 - Follow-ups to be done (ANM / CHO 3 - Follow-ups to be done)

Jurisdiction Activation: Visible for ANMs/CHOs once block or district authorities assign/route an AWC or village cluster list.
Three Scheduling Tracks:
🔴 Track 1: Immediate 7-Day Window — Urgent doctor/MO clinical evaluation at CHC for critical warning signs.
📅 Track 2: Next PMSMA Session at PHC — Scheduled on the 9th, 15th, or 21st (whichever comes first) for comprehensive specialist checkups.
👥 Track 3: Community VHSND Session — Village Health, Sanitation, and Nutrition Day session by local ANM.
Standardized Status Triad:
Complete (Green)
Pending (Amber)
Not Reachable (Blue/Gray with logged attempt timestamp, e.g. "Last dialed 10:15 AM - Switch off")
One-tap actions to Mark Complete, Not Reachable, or Call Mother / ASHA Sangini.


4. Block Nodal Authority: HRP Helpdesk Dashboard (First Page)-- going to similar as BHM for now ( but BHM IS GOING TO HAVE THE ANALYSIS PART TOO ALSO OF HIS BLOCK WHICH IS A NEW SECTION WE WILL ADD AFTERWARDS)
Screen: Block Nodal Authority 1 - HRP Helpdesk Dashboard (Block Nodal Authority 1 - HRP Helpdesk Dashboard)

Block Nodal Point Indicators: Block Shivrajpur CHC Nodal Unit #04 live sync status.
KPI Metrics: 184 Total HRPs Identified, 46 Pending Follow-ups, 28 Next PMSMA Cohort (15th Oct), and 82.4% Compliance Rate.
Three-Track Triangulation Engine: Visual progress for Track 1 (18 due / 4 breached), Track 2 (24 due for 15th Oct PMSMA), and Track 3 (32 pending AWC circles).
Push AWC / ANM Dispatch Box: Allows the Block Nodal officer to push filtered case lists directly into specific ANMs' and CHOs' mobile follow-up panels.
5. Block Nodal Authority: "Follow-up to be done" Panel
Screen: Block Nodal Authority 2 - Follow-up to be done Panel (Block Nodal Authority 2 - Follow-up to be done Panel)

Multi-Tier Shared Line List: Displays all referred HRP cases across the block.
Shared Attribution Tracking: Shows who conducted the follow-up across all tiers:
Done by ANM (Radha Sharma)
Done by CHO (Dr. S. Verma)
Done by HRP_Helpdesk (Amit)
Unassigned / Pending Field Outreach
Real-time Status Updating: Dropdown selector per row to toggle between Pending, Complete, and Not Reachable with audit logging.
Multi-parameter filters by status, tracking pathway, and sub-center/village.


---------- GO WITH THE WHOLE THINGS AND TRY TO UPDATE OR SEE CURRENTLY THINGS ARE LIKE THAT ONLY OR TRY TO FIX @frontend-ui-engineering

skills.name: frontend-ui-engineering
skills.text:
# Skill: frontend-ui-engineering # Frontend UI Engineering ## Overview Build production-quality user interfaces that are accessible, performant, and visually polished. The goal is UI that looks like it was built by a design-aware engineer at a top company — not like it was generated by an AI. This means real design system adherence, proper accessibility, thoughtful interaction patterns, and no generic "AI aesthetic." ## When to Use - Building new UI components or pages - Modifying existing user-facing interfaces - Implementing responsive layouts - Adding interactivity or state management - Fixing visual or UX issues ## Component Architecture ### File Structure Colocate everything related to a component: ``` src/components/ TaskList/ TaskList.tsx # Component implementation TaskList.test.tsx # Tests TaskList.stories.tsx # Storybook stories (if using) use-task-list.ts # Custom hook (if complex state) types.ts # Component-specific types (if needed) ``` ### Component Patterns **Prefer composition over configuration:** ```tsx // Good: Composable Tasks // Avoid: Over-configured } /> ``` **Keep components focused:** ```tsx // Good: Does one thing export function TaskItem({ task, onToggle, onDelete }: TaskItemProps) { return (
  • onToggle(task.id)} /> {task.title}
    • ); } ``` **Separate data fetching from presentation:** ```tsx // Container: handles data export function TaskListContainer() { const { tasks, isLoading, error, refetch } = useTasks(); if (isLoading) return ; if (error) return ; if (tasks.length === 0) return ; return ; } // Presentation: handles rendering export function TaskList({ tasks }: { tasks: Task[] }) { return (
      {tasks.map(task => )}
    ); } ``` ## State Management **Choose the simplest approach that works:** ``` Local state (useState) → Component-specific UI state Lifted state → Shared between 2-3 sibling components Context → Theme, auth, locale (read-heavy, write-rare) URL state (searchParams) → Filters, pagination, shareable UI state Server state (React Query, SWR) → Remote data with caching Global store (Zustand, Redux) → Complex client state shared app-wide ``` **Avoid prop drilling deeper than 3 levels.** If you're passing props through components that don't use them, introduce context or restructure the component tree. ## Design System Adherence ### Reference-led UI quality When the product needs a distinct visual direction, collect evidence before choosing a layout: 1. Search a trusted reference catalogue or use references supplied by the product team. 2. Study two or three relevant screens. Record decisions about hierarchy, density, navigation, controls, responsive behavior, and interaction states. 3. Turn those decisions into a short design contract before implementation. Name the screen's job, primary action, required states, responsive rules, and patterns to reject. 4. Rebuild the useful structure in the product's own components, tokens, content, and visual language. Never copy another product's branding, proprietary text, imagery, or exact layout. Use references as evidence, not as templates. If references are unavailable, document the assumptions and verify the result against the product's existing design system. ### Avoid the AI Aesthetic AI-generated UI has recognizable patterns. Avoid all of them: | AI Default | Why It Is a Problem | Production Quality | |---|---|---| | Purple/indigo everything | Models default to visually "safe" palettes, making every app look identical | Use the project's actual color palette | | Excessive gradients | Gradients add visual noise and clash with most design systems | Flat or subtle gradients matching the design system | | Rounded everything (rounded-2xl) | Maximum rounding signals "friendly" but ignores the hierarchy of corner radii in real designs | Consistent border-radius from the design system | | Generic hero sections | Template-driven layout with no connection to the actual content or user need | Content-first layouts | | Lorem ipsum-style copy | Placeholder text hides layout problems that real content reveals (length, wrapping, overflow) | Realistic placeholder content | | Oversized padding everywhere | Equal generous padding destroys visual hierarchy and wastes screen space | Consistent spacing scale | | Stock card grids | Uniform grids are a layout shortcut that ignores information priority and scanning patterns | Purpose-driven layouts | | Shadow-heavy design | Layered shadows add depth that competes with content and slows rendering on low-end devices | Subtle or no shadows unless the design system specifies | ### Spacing and Layout Use a consistent spacing scale. Don't invent values: ```css /* Use the scale: 0.25rem increments (or whatever the project uses) */ /* Good */ padding: 1rem; /* 16px */ /* Good */ gap: 0.75rem; /* 12px */ /* Bad */ padding: 13px; /* Not on any scale */ /* Bad */ margin-top: 2.3rem; /* Not on any scale */ ``` ### Typography Respect the type hierarchy: ``` h1 → Page title (one per page) h2 → Section title h3 → Subsection title body → Default text small → Secondary/helper text ``` Don't skip heading levels. Don't use heading styles for non-heading content. ### Color - Use semantic color tokens: `text-primary`, `bg-surface`, `border-default` — not raw hex values - Ensure sufficient contrast (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text) - Don't rely solely on color to convey information (use icons, text, or patterns too) ## Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) Every component must meet these standards: ### Keyboard Navigation ```tsx // Every interactive element must be keyboard accessible // ✓ Focusable by default
    Click me
    // ✗ Not focusable
    onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') handleClick(); if (e.key === ' ') e.preventDefault(); }} onKeyUp={e => { if (e.key === ' ') handleClick(); }}> Click me
    ``` ### ARIA Labels ```tsx // Label interactive elements that lack visible text // Label form inputs // Or use aria-label when no visible label exists ``` ### Focus Management ```tsx // Move focus when content changes function Dialog({ isOpen, onClose }: DialogProps) { const closeRef = useRef(null); useEffect(() => { if (isOpen) closeRef.current?.focus(); }, [isOpen]); // Trap focus inside dialog when open return ( {/* dialog content */} ); } ``` ### Meaningful Empty and Error States ```tsx // Don't show blank screens function TaskList({ tasks }: { tasks: Task[] }) { if (tasks.length === 0) { return (

    No tasks

    Get started by creating a new task.

    ); } return
      ...
    ; } ``` ## Responsive Design Design for mobile first, then expand: ```tsx // Tailwind: mobile-first responsive
    ``` Test at these breakpoints: 320px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px. ## Loading and Transitions ```tsx // Skeleton loading (not spinners for content) function TaskListSkeleton() { return (
    {Array.from({ length: 3 }).map((_, i) => (
    ))}
    ); } // Optimistic updates for perceived speed function useToggleTask() { const queryClient = useQueryClient(); return useMutation({ mutationFn: toggleTask, onMutate: async (taskId) => { await queryClient.cancelQueries({ queryKey: ['tasks'] }); const previous = queryClient.getQueryData(['tasks']); queryClient.setQueryData(['tasks'], (old: Task[]) => old.map(t => t.id === taskId ? { ...t, done: !t.done } : t) ); return { previous }; }, onError: (_err, _taskId, context) => { queryClient.setQueryData(['tasks'], context?.previous); }, }); } ``` ## See Also For detailed accessibility requirements and testing tools, see `../../references/accessibility-checklist.md`. ## Common Rationalizations | Rationalization | Reality | |---|---| | "Accessibility is a nice-to-have" | It's a legal requirement in many jurisdictions and an engineering quality standard. | | "We'll make it responsive later" | Retrofitting responsive design is 3x harder than building it from the start. | | "The design isn't final, so I'll skip styling" | Use the design system defaults. Unstyled UI creates a broken first impression for reviewers. | | "This is just a prototype" | Prototypes become production code. Build the foundation right. | | "The AI aesthetic is fine for now" | It signals low quality. Use the project's actual design system from the start. | ## Red Flags - Components with more than 200 lines (split them) - Inline styles or arbitrary pixel values - Missing error states, loading states, or empty states - No keyboard navigation testing - Color as the sole indicator of state (red/green without text or icons) - Generic "AI look" (purple gradients, oversized cards, stock layouts) ## Verification After building UI: - [ ] Component renders without console errors - [ ] All interactive elements are keyboard accessible (Tab through the page) - [ ] Screen reader can convey the page's content and structure - [ ] Responsive: works at 320px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px - [ ] Loading, empty, error, success, and permission states handled when applicable - [ ] Follows the project's design system (spacing, colors, typography) - [ ] The rendered result passes a final UI-specific finish-gate review - [ ] No accessibility warnings in dev tools or axe-core Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\ADITYA\.config\opencode\skills\frontend-ui-engineering Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory. import type { HrpComplication } from "./types.js";
```ts
import type { HrpReason } from "./hrp-reasons.js";

export const HRP_COMPLICATIONS: { value: HrpComplication; label: string }[] = [
  { value: "ANEMIA", label: "Anemia" },
  { value: "PIH", label: "PIH (Pregnancy-Induced Hypertension)" },
  { value: "GDM", label: "GDM (Gestational Diabetes Mellitus)" },
  { value: "SHORT_STATURE", label: "Short stature" },
  { value: "PRE_LSCS", label: "Pre-LSCS" },
  { value: "MULTI_GRAVIDA", label: "Multi gravida" },
  { value: "TWINS_MULTIPLE_PREGNANCY", label: "Twins / Multiple Pregnancy" },
  { value: "TEENAGE_PREGNANCY", label: "Teenage Pregnancy" },
  { value: "EDEMA", label: "Edema" },
];

export function getHrpComplicationLabel(v) {...}

const REASON_BY_COMPLICATION: Record<HrpComplication, HrpReason> = {
  ANEMIA: "SEVERE_ANEMIA",
  PIH: "HYPERTENSION",
  GDM: "GESTATIONAL_DIABETES",
  SHORT_STATURE: "SHORT_STATURE",
  PRE_LSCS: "PREVIOUS_C_SECTION",
  MULTI_GRAVIDA: "BAD_OBSTETRIC_HISTORY",

  EDEMA: "HYPERTENSION",   // edema is a PIH warning sign
};
export function hrpReasonForComplication(c) { return REASON_BY_COMPLICATION[c]; }
```

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Rebuild the HRP tracking app's navigation and screens around the requested role hierarchy: ANM/CHO field app (Add case → Dashboard → Follow-ups), Block Nodal (BHM) / DHS oversight app (Dashboard → Follow-up to be done → Add HRP case → Team & access), including a 7-field HRP intake form, three-track follow-up panels, shared attribution line list, block KPI dashboard with dispatch box, and email/password provisioning of HRP Helpdesk accounts.

## Requirements
- ANM & CHO page order: 1) Add case (first screen), 2) Dashboard (triage/urgent counts), 3) "Follow-up to be done" (only when lists are assigned from block/district).
- ANM/CHO first screen: one large Add button dominating the page, plus a critical instruction strip at the bottom (Sync now / urgent HRP follow-up). Clicking Add opens the 7-field form.
- 7 fields exactly: Name (Aadhaar/MCP guidance), Mobile (clean 10-digit with +91 prefix), Age (completed years), Village mapped to HWC (dropdown), LMP (auto EDD + gestational-age badge), Complication dropdown with exact 9 options (Anemia, PIH, GDM, Short stature, Pre-LSCS, Multi gravida, Twins / Multiple Pregnancy, Teenage Pregnancy, Edema), Referring or Not? (Yes — Refer to CHC/FRU, escalates to Block Nodal HRP Helpdesk and BHM panel; No — Routine Field Management).
- Follow-up panel: three tracks — Track 1 immediate 7-day MO evaluation; Track 2 next PMSMA session (9th/15th/21st, whichever first); Track 3 VHSND community session. Status triad Complete (green) / Pending (amber) / Not Reachable (blue-gray with last-attempt timestamp). One-tap Mark Complete, Not Reachable, Call Mother / ASHA Sangini.
- Block Nodal (and same for BHM): dashboard with block nodal point/live sync status, KPIs (Total HRPs, Pending Follow-ups, Next PMSMA Cohort, Compliance Rate), three-track triangulation, and a "Push AWC / ANM Dispatch Box" to push filtered lists into ANM/CHO panels.
- Block Nodal "Follow-up to be done": all-persons shared line list with attribution (Done by ANM / CHO / HRP_Helpdesk / Unassigned), per-row status dropdown with audit logging, filters by status, track, and sub-center/village.
- Block Nodal page 4: create/assign the HRP Helpdesk role using email + password; only that person's credentials grant access.
- BHM will gain a separate block-analysis section later — do not build it now.
- Follow the frontend-ui-engineering quality bar (real design tokens, accessibility, no generic AI aesthetic, loading/empty/error states).

## Decisions
- Add new role `HELPDESK` to `UserRole` (used for HRP Helpdesk operators), rather than overloading BHM/CHO.
- Add nullable `users.email` with case-insensitive unique index; login accepts either employee ID or email (same `employeeId` form field).
- Helpers: `BHM` and `DHS` may provision only `HELPDESK` accounts, scoped to their facility subtree.
- New authz actions `followup:manage` (status updates + dispatch) and `staff:manage` (provision helpdesk).
- Village selection stores the facility name in `patient.address`; patient facility remains server-derived. No DB column added for village.
- Complication maps to existing risk-engine `hrpReason` via `hrpReasonForComplication` so HRP registrations score AMBER+.
- HRP patient creation auto-creates a `follow_ups` row using `scheduleFollowUp`, assigned to the registering user; block can re-dispatch.
- Client line list merges server `follow_ups` records with the patient register, falling back to `patient.followUpTrack` / `inferHrpTrack` so demo/legacy data still renders.
- Route semantics: `/` is role-aware home (ANM/CHO → FieldHome big Add button; oversight → NodalDashboard); `/dashboard` = field triage dashboard; `/follow-ups` = role-aware panel; `/patients/new` = 7-field intake; `/team` = Team & access.
- CHO now receives the field dashboard (previously oversight), matching the stated spec; its existing oversight tools remain in nav overflow.

## Work State
### Completed
- Shared package updated: `UserRole` += `HELPDESK`; `HrpComplication` += `EDEMA` (now 9); `UserSchema.email`; new `hrp-complications.ts` (labels/hints + reason mapping) and `hrp-follow-up.ts` (track/status metadata, `inferHrpTrack`); schemas now export `FollowUpListItem`, `DispatchFollowUpSchema`, `CreateStaffSchema`, `StaffMemberSchema`; `HrpPatientFilterSchema` reuses `HrpComplication`; index exports new modules.
- Server migration `006_hrp_helpdesk.sql` (email column, unique index, role check incl. HELPDESK, follow-up index).
- Server `db/types.ts` User.email; `serializers.ts` emits email; `auth.ts` login by employee ID or lowercase email.
- Server authz: `policy.ts` adds `staff:manage`/`followup:manage`, HELPDESK in clinical-write and referral destinations, `canManageFollowUp`/`canManageStaff`; `scope.ts` HELPDESK → BLOCK/CHC.
- New `routes/staff.ts` (GET list, POST create HELPDESK with bcrypt + generated `HD-XXXXXXXX` employee ID, PATCH `/:id/deactivate`), registered at `/api/staff` in `app.ts`.
- `routes/follow-ups.ts`: list now joins completed-by user and returns patient/attribution context via `toFollowUpListItem`; new `POST /dispatch`; PATCH now uses `followup:manage`.
- `routes/hrp.ts`: derives `hrpReason` from complication and auto-creates patient track + `follow_ups` row on HRP registration.
- `db/seed.ts`: deletes new tables in safe order, adds HELPDESK user `HELP01` (`helpdesk.daskroi@araria.gov.in` / `password123`), sets `is_hrp`/complication/track/status on patients, inserts 4 follow-up rows with ANM/CHO/Helpdesk attribution, inserts block/district nodal designations, prints helpdesk credentials.
- Client `lib/api.ts`: adds `api.hrp.patients` (list/get/create/update), `api.hrp.followUps` (list/field/panel/update/dispatch), `api.staff` (list/create/deactivate).
- Client `lib/nav.ts` rewritten with field vs oversight navigation, `isFieldRole`/`isNodalRole`, role-based nav arrays, titles.
- Client `lib/session.ts` adds `useIsFieldRole`, `useIsNodalRole`, `ROLE_LABEL` with HELPDESK, `ROLE_TIER_LABEL`, `tierLabel`; `useCanWriteClinical` includes HELPDESK.
- Client `lib/hrp.ts` created: EDD/GA helpers, `FollowUpRow`, `buildFollowUpLineList`, `isBreached`, `summariseFollowUps`, `attributionLabel`, `formatShortDate`.
- `pages/AddPatient.tsx` rewritten as the 7-field intake (phone with +91, village select, EDD/GA badges, complication select, referral radio cards, submits via `api.hrp.patients.create`, navigates to `/follow-ups`).
- `pages/FieldHome.tsx` created (big Add button, urgent/sync bottom strip).

### Active
- Building remaining client screens: role-aware FollowUps split (field panel + nodal shared line list with status dropdown/attribution/filters), NodalDashboard (KPIs, three-track triangulation, dispatch box), TeamAccess (list + create Helpdesk), role-aware App routes, Layout/Login/Settings label updates, Dashboard CHO→field change.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `src/components/follow-ups/FieldFollowUpPanel.tsx` and `NodalFollowUpPanel.tsx`; rewrite `pages/FollowUps.tsx` to switch on `useIsFieldRole()`.
2. Create `pages/NodalDashboard.tsx` (KPIs from `summariseFollowUps`, track cards, dispatch box using `api.staff.list` + `api.hrp.followUps.dispatch`) and `pages/TeamAccess.tsx`.
3. Wire routes in `App.tsx` (`/` role-aware Home, `/dashboard`, `/team`) and update `Layout.tsx` labels (use `ROLE_LABEL`, HELPDESK) and `Login.tsx` copy ("Email or employee ID") + demo credentials.
4. Update `Dashboard.tsx` so CHO uses field view; keep oversight view for BHM/DHS/HELPDESK.
5. Update/add tests: `Layout.test.tsx`, `Dashboard.test.tsx`, `AddPatient.test.tsx`, `FollowUps.test.tsx`; add `lib/hrp.test.ts`, `pages/FieldHome.test.tsx`, `pages/NodalDashboard.test.tsx`, `pages/TeamAccess.test.tsx`; update `server/src/authz/policy.test.ts` (add HELPDESK actor/facility + expected `followup:manage`/`staff:manage`) and `shared/src/types.test.ts` (five roles).
6. Run `npm run build --workspace=packages/shared`, then `npm run check:fast`, `npm test`, `npm run coverage`, `npm run check:changed-coverage`; fix type/lint/coverage failures.

## Relevant Files
- `packages/client/src/App.tsx`: routes still need role-aware `/`, `/dashboard`, `/team`.
- `packages/client/src/pages/FollowUps.tsx`: still the old ANC-derived page; must be replaced by role-aware panels.
- `packages/client/src/components/Layout.tsx`: has its own `ROLE_LABEL` map needing HELPDESK; renders nav/tabbar/More sheet.
- `packages/client/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx`: role branch currently `role === "ANM"` only; long file with `OversightDashboard`.
- `packages/client/src/lib/hrp.ts`: new line-list/KPI/attribution helpers used by panels and dashboard.
- `packages/client/src/lib/nav.ts`: source of role navigation and page titles.
- `packages/client/src/pages/AddPatient.tsx`: new 7-field intake; existing test must be rewritten.
- `packages/client/src/lib/api.ts`: new `hrp` and `staff` clients.
- `packages/server/src/routes/follow-ups.ts`: list context, dispatch, status PATCH.
- `packages/server/src/routes/staff.ts`: helpdesk provisioning.
- `packages/server/src/authz/policy.ts` + `policy.test.ts`: new actions and role matrix.
- `packages/server/migrations/006_hrp_helpdesk.sql`: email/role/index migration.
- `packages/server/src/db/seed.ts`: demo users, HRP flags, follow-ups, nodal designations.
- `packages/shared/src/hrp-follow-up.ts` + `hrp-complications.ts`: track/status/complication metadata.
- `scripts/check-changed-coverage.mjs`: changed-line coverage gate (`>=80%`).

## Important Context
- Nothing is committed; all changes are in the working tree.
- Login field is still named `employeeId` in `LoginSchema`; server accepts email in that field. Label should read "Email or employee ID".
- `FollowUpListItem` is a TS interface (not zod) carrying `patientName/age/phone/riskLevel/hrpComplication/village/assignedToName/assignedToRole/completedByName/completedByRole`; `/hrp/follow-ups` list returns it, `/field` and `/panel` still return older shapes.
- `getNextPmsmaDate`, `getNextVhsndDate`, `addDays`, `scheduleFollowUp`, `inferHrpTrack` come from `@hrp/shared`; client alias maps `@hrp/shared` to `packages/shared/src`.
- Server unit coverage excludes integration tests and has no coverage records for most route files, so new route code is listed as "no coverage data" rather than failing the changed-line gate; `policy.ts` and shared/client files do count and need tests.
- Existing demo patients in seed now have `is_hrp` set and 4 `follow_ups` rows; reseeding requires `npm run db:seed` against Docker Postgres.
- `/hrp/follow-ups/dispatch` accepts `{ patientIds, assignedToUserId, track, scheduledDate?, notes? }`, only ANM/CHO/HELPDESK assignees, and defaults the scheduled date per track.
- Constraint floor: no `@ts-ignore`, `eslint-disable`, `# noqa`, empty `catch`, stubs, skipped tests, or secrets; do not weaken `CONSTRAINTS.md`.
